author: product-requirements-expert
title: Correct a booked visit's date and description
summary: A booked visit can be corrected: its date and description are changed after booking, validated as a booking is (description required, date later than today), updating the existing visit in place with no new visit added. Success shows the owner's record; refusal redisplays the correction form. Cancelling a booked visit stays out of scope.
acceptance_criteria: Opening the correction form for a booked visit shows the form carrying that visit's current date and description
Submitting a valid description and a date later than today as a correction updates that visit in place, adds no additional visit to the pet, and shows the owner's record
A correction with a blank description is refused, names the description, and redisplays the correction form
A correction with a date of today or earlier is refused, names the date, and redisplays the correction form
non_goals: A visible entry point or edit link from the owner's record (deferred; see Open Questions)
notes: REQ-VIS-003 narrows NG-5; decision recorded in docs/adr/2026-08-27-non-goal-cancel-visit.md. Narrowest-reading choices taken and left open for design to confirm: (1) the correction is reachable by direct navigation only, with no owner-page link in this slice; (2) a correction targeting a visit whose pet does not belong to the named owner is refused, mirroring Visits edge case 1. ADR README index needs a row for the new non-goal ADR, added by that file's owner (out of my write scope).

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The visit-correction flow reuses the established controller-based in-place update pattern verbatim. It mirrors PetController's edit pair (GET/POST /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/edit): the GET returns the shared form with the aggregate-loaded entity prefilled, the POST binds the submission onto that same managed instance, runs bean-validation plus a controller cross-field check, and cascade-saves through the Owner aggregate root (system-design Contracts; ADR 2026-08-08 feature-package-organization; ADR 2026-08-27-non-goal-cancel-visit records the product decision). No new module, layer, pattern, or dependency. Basis: grep/Read of PetController.java (initUpdateForm/processUpdateForm/updatePetDetails), VisitController.java (loadPetWithVisit/processNewVisitForm), Owner.getPet(Integer)/addVisit, Pet.getVisits/addVisit, Visit (@NotBlank description) — IDE oracle not connected, so this is the weaker grep-based basis.
integration_points: New routes GET+POST /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit on the existing VisitController; both reuse the pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm template and its 'visit' model attribute (no template change required — the form posts back to the same URL it was served from).

Extend the existing @ModelAttribute('visit') loadPetWithVisit to take @PathVariable(name='visitId', required=false) Integer visitId, mirroring PetController.findPet's optional petId: when visitId is null keep today's behavior (new Visit, pet.addVisit); when present, return the existing managed Visit located on the pet WITHOUT calling addVisit, so form binding mutates it in place and no extra visit is created.
Add Pet.getVisit(Integer id) iterating getVisits() and matching by identity (visits are EAGER-fetched), mirroring Owner.getPet(Integer id). This is the one genuinely new symbol.

POST handler: run the same non-future date check used by processNewVisitForm (result.rejectValue('date','typeMismatch.visitDate')), then on success this.owners.save(owner) (cascade persists the mutated Visit) and redirect:/owners/{ownerId} with a flash message; on result.hasErrors() return the form view unchanged.
No owner-page link is added in this slice (see notes) — the route is reached by direct navigation only.

patterns.description: initUpdateForm/processUpdateForm/updatePetDetails — the template for GET-prefill + POST in-place mutation of an existing aggregate member, cascade-saved through OwnerRepository, redirect-on-success/redisplay-on-failure. The visit edit is the same shape with the Visit member.
findPet with @PathVariable(required=false): new-vs-existing branch driven by presence of the id path variable. loadPetWithVisit gains the identical visitId branch.
Owner.getPet(Integer id) identity lookup over a cascaded collection — the exact shape Pet.getVisit(Integer id) mirrors.

risks.risk: Ownership/containment guard must refuse a visitId whose Visit is not under the named owner's pet (mirror Visits edge case 1 at visit granularity).
risks.mitigation: loadPetWithVisit already throws IllegalArgumentException when owner.getPet(petId) is null (pet-not-under-owner). Extend the same fail-closed guard: when pet.getVisit(visitId) returns null, throw IllegalArgumentException. This is a malformed/forbidden request, not user form-data — keep it as a thrown refusal (consistent with the existing owner-not-found and pet-not-found guards), distinct from the blank-description/past-date validation failures which redisplay the form.

risks.risk: In-place update must add no second visit record (acceptance criterion + test correctingVisitShouldUpdateInPlaceWithoutAddingVisit).
risks.mitigation: The edit path returns the existing managed Visit from loadPetWithVisit and never calls pet.addVisit/owner.addVisit; binding mutates the loaded instance and owners.save cascades the update. addVisit is confined to the visitId==null branch.

risks.risk: Mass-assignment of the visit identity via the form.
risks.mitigation: The existing @InitBinder setDisallowedFields('id','*.id') already blocks it; the id is carried by the loaded managed instance, not by the form.

notes: Open question (1) CONFIRMED as narrowed: no owner-page edit link in this slice. Consistent with the 2026-08-27-non-goal-cancel-visit ADR (link left as an open question) and the prd-entry non_goal. The route is reachable by direct URL only; adding the link is a trivial, independently-shippable follow-up and needs no design change here. Open question (2) CONFIRMED and made precise: refuse a correction whose visit's pet is not under the named owner. Realize it as a thrown IllegalArgumentException in loadPetWithVisit at two levels — pet-not-under-owner (already present) and visit-not-under-pet (new, via pet.getVisit(visitId)==null). This mirrors Visits edge case 1 and matches the controller's existing fail-closed guard style; it is deliberately NOT a form redisplay, because a mismatched identity is a malformed request rather than an invalid user entry. author: code-quality-reviewer

findings.description: Pet.getVisit(Integer id) returns null when no matching visit exists. The checklist mandates Optional for nullable return values, not null. The inconsistency is sharpest inside the same method body that consumes this result (VisitController.loadPetWithVisit): the owner lookup one line earlier uses owners.findById(ownerId).orElseThrow(...), the idiomatic Optional chain, while the visit lookup two lines later falls back to an explicit null check. A reader must shift idioms mid-method. Note that Owner.getPet(Integer id) (pre-existing, outside the changeset) carries the same anti-pattern; the fix to Pet.getVisit should extend to Owner.getPet for consistency, since fixing only the new method would preserve the asymmetry.
findings.fix: Change the return type of Pet.getVisit to Optional<Visit> and return Optional.empty() instead of null. Update VisitController.loadPetWithVisit to call pet.getVisit(visitId).orElseThrow(() -> new IllegalArgumentException(...)).

findings.description: The intermediate variable 'compId' in getVisit captures visit.getId() and is used exactly once on the immediately following line. The variable adds a name without adding clarity — 'compId' says nothing that 'visit.getId()' does not already say at the call site.
findings.fix: Inline the expression: collapse the two lines to Objects.equals(visit.getId(), id).

Ownership guard is present and consistent: loadPetWithVisit verifies owner, then pet, then visit before returning — matching the depth of the existing new-visit path.
Optional visitId path variable correctly extends the shared @ModelAttribute method to serve both new and edit routes without duplicating owner/pet load logic.
processUpdateVisitForm omits @PathVariable petId (not needed for edit path, correctly minimal).
Date validation is identical to processNewVisitForm, satisfying REQ-VIS-003 validated-exactly-as-a-booking requirement.
The edit path does not call pet.addVisit — the returned visit is already in the collection, so save cascades the update in place, meeting the no-additional-visit acceptance criterion by construction.
Four new tests cover all four REQ-VIS-003 acceptance criteria: GET shows current values, POST success redirects, POST with blank description refused, POST with past date refused.
Test names follow BDD sentence style and communicate the scenario without requiring the body to be read.

correctingVisitShouldUpdateInPlaceWithoutAddingVisit asserts pet.getVisits().hasSize(1) — a structural check that would catch a regression invisible to redirect-only assertions.
Package placement correct: all changes stay within org.springframework.samples.petclinic.owner.

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: All four new test methods are missing the `the` prefix mandated by the project's BDD naming school (`the{Subject}Should{Outcome}`), which applies to all tests written from 2026-07-31 onward. Current names: `editVisitFormShouldShowCurrentDateAndDescription`, `correctingVisitShouldUpdateInPlaceWithoutAddingVisit`, `correctionWithBlankDescriptionShouldBeRefusedAndRedisplayForm`, `correctionWithPastDateShouldBeRefusedAndRedisplayForm`. The school says the subject leads with `the` so the name reads as a specification sentence.

The description assertion uses the bare string literal `"Annual checkup"` rather than `booked.getDescription()`. The date assertion on the preceding line correctly uses `booked.getDate()` (derived from the returned visit object). The description breaks the Derived Expectations principle (testing-principles.md): the expected value should be derived from the named input, not repeated as a magic string that silently stays green if both sides are changed together.

`correctionWithPastDateShouldBeRefusedAndRedisplayForm` submits `LocalDate.now()` (today), which is the boundary value the PRD names ("today or earlier"), not a past date. The name says "past date" but exercises "today" — the boundary case. The analogous existing test is named `processNewVisitFormHasErrorsWhenVisitDateIsNotInFuture`, which describes the condition precisely. A reader following the name alone would expect a date before today, not today itself.
findings.fix: Rename to `theCorrectionWithNonFutureDateShouldBeRefusedAndRedisplayForm` (which also picks up the `the` prefix fix above).

recommendations: No test exercises the visit ownership-mismatch guard: `VisitController.java:84-88` throws `IllegalArgumentException` when `pet.getVisit(visitId)` returns null (visit not under the named pet). The design-block at line 8 identifies this as an explicit risk and mitigation. The prd-entry does not name a test for this path, and the analogous pet-not-under-owner guard also lacks a test in the pre-existing suite, so this is a recommendation rather than a required change. Adding a test that submits an edit request for a visitId not belonging to the pet and asserts a 4xx or error response would close the gap.
approved_aspects: All four acceptance criteria from the prd-entry are covered by a dedicated test: form prefill, update-in-place, blank-description refusal, and non-future-date refusal

The update-in-place test correctly asserts `pet.getVisits().hasSize(1)` and `updated.getId() == TEST_VISIT_ID` — non-tautological: the assertion would catch any code path that called `addVisit` and added a second visit record

Mocking: @WebMvcTest + @MockitoBean for OwnerRepository is the established class pattern; `verify(this.owners).save(this.owner)` is consistent with that prior art and within the brief's tolerated-mock-framework exception

AssertJ fluent assertions (`assertThat(...).hasSize(1)`, `.isEqualTo(...)`) used correctly in the update test; Hamcrest `hasProperty`/`is` in the model attribute matchers is forced by the MockMvc result-matcher API and is acceptable
`givenBookedVisit` factory method wraps Visit construction correctly; test bodies do not call `new Visit()` directly
Tests are straight-line, independent, and phase-separated; no branching or loops in test bodies
All seven tests in the class pass (confirmed by gradlew test run)

author: code-quality-reviewer

findings.description: isPresent() + get() antipattern in updatePetDetails. The code assigns Optional<Pet> existingPet = owner.getPet(id), then branches on existingPet.isPresent() and calls existingPet.get() inside. This reconstructs a null-check in Optional clothing and defeats Optional's purpose. The idiomatic Java form for a present-or-else split with a side-effecting else branch is ifPresentOrElse: owner.getPet(id).ifPresentOrElse(target -> { target.setName(pet.getName()); target.setBirthDate(pet.getBirthDate()); target.setType(pet.getType()); }, () -> owner.addPet(pet));
findings.fix: Replace the isPresent()/get() block with owner.getPet(id).ifPresentOrElse(target -> { target.setName(...); target.setBirthDate(...); target.setType(...); }, () -> owner.addPet(pet)); and remove the local variable existingPet entirely.

summary: A booked visit can be corrected: its date and description are changed after booking, validated as a booking is (description required, date later than today), updating the existing visit in place with no new visit added.
